chapter: Trent's band: touring, sidemen and breakup
title: Memphis Casino date, Cab Calloway and the awful South
summary: A missed big job at the Casino in Memphis, following Cab Calloway, and Memphis was awful for Black bands.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: I know Dan Minor told me he left to go to Benny Moller (phonetic spelling). Benny Moller was starting to try to raid your band, when you missed that job, you were late for that job in the Casino Ballroom in Memphis, somebody said you had an accident on the road; this was a big job, it was supposed to be for something like six weeks and you were opening on New Year's Eve or some big holiday--Christmas.
We didn't miss too much because we followed Cab Calloway and Cab had a lot
Cab had a lot of trouble?
They had locked him in the Memphis office. Memphis used to be awful. It used to be awful. It's a wonderful country today, Frank, but it used to be (inaudible)
I wouldn't have wanted to play the south for anything in the world in those days.
In those days the south was awful.
You guys never played in the Carolinas or any of that part of the country at all?
In fact, Memphis was the only place you played in Tennessee.

I recall Claude Williams telling me it was such a great band and you had such a hard time. You'd get a job and then something would happen and you'd be out of work for a while, then you'd get another job. It was hard to keep the band together the last couple of years.
